events.title: Trump Administration Removes Habitat Protection from Endangered Species Act Definition of 'Harm'
events.one_liner: The Trump administration finalized a rule on July 10 removing habitat destruction from the regulatory definition of "harm" under the Endangered Species Act, effective September 14. The change weakens protections for endangered species by allowing farming, drilling, mining, logging, and development to proceed in critical habitats without violating the law, overturning a 30-year legal interpretation upheld by the Supreme Court.
takeaways: Habitat destruction no longer counts as illegal 'take' under the Endangered Species Act as of September 14, 2026
The rule removes decades-old regulatory language that treated severe habitat damage as 'harm' to protected wildlife
Direct injury and killing remain prohibited, but habitat loss outside designated critical habitat areas now receives no ESA protection
The change applies to private projects with no federal funding or permits, limiting federal agency consultation requirements
The decision reverses the 1995 Supreme Court ruling in Babbitt v. Sweet Home that protected habitat as part of species protection

events.title: Ketogenic Diet Improves Exercise Response in High Blood Sugar, Study Finds
events.one_liner: A new study led by exercise researcher Sarah Lessard found that a high-fat, low-carbohydrate ketogenic diet helped mice with high blood sugar normalize glucose levels and dramatically improved how their muscles responded to exercise, enhancing oxygen uptake and endurance capacity.
takeaways: Study published Feb. 25 in Nature Communications by Sarah Lessard at Virginia Tech's Fralin Biomedical Research Institute
Mice on ketogenic diet normalized blood sugar within one week
Diet caused muscle remodeling, increasing oxidative fibers and aerobic exercise response
High blood sugar normally impairs muscles' ability to increase oxygen uptake during exercise; ketogenic diet counteracted this effect

events.title: Cisco Secure Email Threat Defense Achieves FedRAMP Class D (High) Certification
events.one_liner: Cisco announced on August 10, 2026, that its Secure Email Threat Defense solution has achieved FedRAMP Class D (High) certification, meeting the U.S. government's most rigorous security standards. This milestone enables the solution to protect federal agencies and contractors handling classified and regulated data with continuous monitoring and federally authorized security controls.
takeaways: FedRAMP Class D (High) certification achieved August 10, 2026
Requires continuous third-party monitoring and assessment, not one-time authorization
Provides AI-powered detection with API-based or inline gateway-level protection modes
Enables compliance for agencies and contractors handling controlled unclassified information (CUI)
